name: cli
description: Cross-cutting CLI infrastructure. Provides the root command, version subcommand, and subcommand registration framework using cobra.

requirements.title: Root command and subcommand registration
requirements.description: A top-level cobra root command that the binary's entry point attaches the module subcommands onto, sets global flags, and prints help when invoked with no args.

requirements.title: Version command
requirements.description: A `spex version` subcommand that prints version string and build info injected at build time via ldflags.

requirements.title: Identity hash computation command
requirements.description: `spex hash-id --module <module> --type <type> --name <name>` computes and prints the 12-character hex identity hash for the given spec node. The command calls schema.IdentityHash with the appropriate parts for the node type. Exits 0 with the hash on stdout, exits 1 with a usage error if required flags are missing.

requirements.title: Bounded third-party CLI surface
requirements.description: cobra is the only third-party CLI framework in the binary: no second command library and no hand-rolled argument parser stands beside it, and argument and flag parsing, help text, unknown-command suggestions and shell completions are taken from cobra's built-ins rather than reimplemented. cobra reaches exactly two packages: cli, which holds the root command and nothing else, and cmd/spex, which holds all twelve subcommand constructors, one per file. No other package imports it — the worker packages that do the module's actual work define no commands and see no CLI framework at all, and a subcommand's run function reads flags into plain Go values before calling into them. What is bounded is therefore both which third-party module may be reached for and how far it reaches: the root command imports cobra and nothing else, and cobra stops at command construction. pflag and mousetrap arrive transitively through cobra and are never imported directly. A subcommand needing a capability cobra does not provide reaches for the standard library; anything else amends the project's declared stack before it is written. The bounded surface is now enumerated in the graph rather than only counted here: each of the twelve constructors' commands is declared as an api node in the module that owns its entry point, plus the three `spex map` children, and the api names are globally unique across the project so no two modules can claim one invocation. The bare `spex` root is deliberately not among them — it runs no operation, only cobra's help, and every capability it does own is a persistent flag or a built-in, none of which is part of an api name.
